mutants.why: the LE length prefix must be all 4 bytes wide; emitting only 3 shifts the body one byte earlier. encode_prefixesLittleEndianLength asserts QCOMPARE(frame.at(4), '{') (fifth byte is the body's opening brace) and QCOMPARE(length, frame.size()-4) -- both fail when the header is 3 bytes.

the length prefix is written little-endian; writing big-endian reverses the 4 length bytes. encode_prefixesLittleEndianLength reads the header back with qFromLittleEndian and asserts QCOMPARE(length, frame.size()-4) -- a byte-swapped header decodes to a huge value, not the body size, so it fails (also breaks roundTrip: the decoder then sees an oversized length).

the 4-byte length prefix is decoded little-endian; decoding big-endian reads the LE-encoded low byte as the high byte, so any real frame decodes to a multi-hundred-MB length that trips the oversize cap. roundTrip_encodeThenParseRecoversObject asserts QCOMPARE(parsed.status, Status::Ok) -- the mutant returns Error/NeedMore instead. Directly covers the LE byte-order requirement.

with exactly 4 bytes present the header is complete and readable; '<=' wrongly treats a full-header-but-empty-body buffer as NeedMore, so a length prefix can never be evaluated at the boundary. parse_zeroLengthIsError feeds a 4-byte buffer and asserts QCOMPARE(status, Status::Error) -- the mutant returns NeedMore instead.

inverting the zero-length fail-closed guard makes every NON-zero length report the 'length is zero' error while a real zero length falls through to an empty-body JSON parse. parse_zeroLengthIsError asserts the error text contains "zero"; with the mutant a zero frame instead errors with "object" (empty body) -- QVERIFY(error.contains("zero")) fails (also breaks roundTrip, whose non-zero length now errors).

inverting the oversize fail-closed guard lets an attacker-supplied over-cap length through (it is no longer > the cap) while rejecting all legitimate small frames. parse_oversizedLengthIsError sends cap+1 and asserts QCOMPARE(status, Status::Error) -- the mutant lets it pass to a NeedMore instead (and roundTrip's normal-size frame is now falsely rejected as oversized).

'>=' rejects a frame whose length is EXACTLY kMaxNativeMessageBytes (a legal max-size frame), differing from '>' only at length==cap. parse_exactlyCapSizedLengthIsAccepted builds a valid JSON-object body of exactly kMaxNativeMessageBytes and asserts QCOMPARE(status, Status::Ok) + consumed==frame.size() -- the mutant rejects it as oversized. (parse_oversizedLengthIsError still pins the cap+1 rejection above.)

'total' is both the completeness threshold and the consumed byte count; dropping 1 makes the decoder report one byte too few consumed, desyncing the stream on the next frame. roundTrip_encodeThenParseRecoversObject asserts QCOMPARE(parsed.consumed, encodeFrame(original).size()) -- the mutant yields size-1 (also caught by parse_multipleFramesConsumedIndividually, whose second frame then starts one byte early).

the payload-availability bounds check must accept a buffer holding exactly one whole frame (size == total); '<=' wrongly reports a complete frame as NeedMore. roundTrip_encodeThenParseRecoversObject (buffer is exactly one frame) asserts QCOMPARE(status, Status::Ok) and parse_multipleFramesConsumedIndividually asserts the trailing exact-fit frame parses Ok -- both fail.

the body slice must be exactly 'length' bytes; taking length-1 truncates the JSON (drops its closing brace) so it no longer parses as an object. roundTrip_encodeThenParseRecoversObject asserts QCOMPARE(parsed.status, Status::Ok) and QCOMPARE(parsed.message, original) -- the truncated body yields an Error instead.

consumed must include the 4-byte length prefix (total = prefix + body); reporting only the body length under-consumes by 4 and desyncs the stream. roundTrip_encodeThenParseRecoversObject asserts QCOMPARE(parsed.consumed, encodeFrame(original).size()) which includes the prefix, and parse_multipleFramesConsumedIndividually removes 'first.consumed' then asserts the second frame parses to b -- both fail (leftover prefix bytes corrupt the next parse).
